description: Average athlete (70kg) — vegetarian dietary preference. Tests solver under food-pool constraint pressure when meat-based foods are excluded.
knownFailureReason: GENUINE ALGORITHM PARITY VIOLATION (sodium): Rule solver produces 220mg sodium vs 800mg target (72.5% miss). Root cause: the rule solver picks 2x gel + 1x sports drink as the carb backbone, exhausting its carb budget, then the electrolyte-fill pass fails to find an electrolyte food that 'improves the score'. The issue is the electrolyte selection logic's scoring function skips addition when there's no improvement, leaving a large sodium gap. In the full production flow (with DB foods), more high-sodium options are available; with the in-memory test catalog this surfaces a real solver gap. CARB issue: 2x gel + sports drink = 65g vs 55g target — the rule solver's minimum-carb selection (1 gel = 25g) + sports drink overshoots 55g with no way to deliver exactly 55g from indivisible servings. TODO: Electrolyte scoring logic should prioritize filling a sodium gap regardless of score improvement when deficit exceeds 30%.
